I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation, because that fits my land, my well irrigation, and the way people farm here. I only have 6 mu and I am already 70, so I will keep the plan simple and not spread myself too thin. Since some family members work off-farm and I have only farmed for 1 year, I will put 4 mu into the main wheat-maize system, then keep 1 mu in cotton and 1 mu in stevia as smaller cash-crop plots that I can still manage. On the wheat and maize land, I will use improved seed and moderate fertilizer so I can get stable yield without pushing costs too hard. I will irrigate wheat more than maize because wheat here responds well to a few key waterings, while maize can rely more on summer rain with one or two well irrigations if needed. For cotton and stevia, I will keep the area small, use improved seed, and manage them more carefully because they need more attention than grain crops. I will use rotary tillage on most plots because it is easier for me to manage than deep ploughing and suits a small farm like mine. My goal this year is steady production, manageable labor, and lower risk rather than chasing the highest possible yield.
